title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and seasons, describe the landscape, and say what is about to happen.
intro:
Kerala has a tropical climate shaped by **two monsoons**: the south-west monsoon (ഇടവപ്പാതി, June–August) and the north-east monsoon (തുലാവർഷം, October–November). Between them come hot, humid summers (March–May) and pleasant cooler months (December–February). Rain is a constant topic of conversation — and of Malayalam poetry and film.

Grammar: Malayalam weather sentences have **no dummy 'it'** — the rain itself 'falls', the wind 'blows'. You'll also learn **-ആൻ പോകുന്നു** 'is going to'.

grammar.title: Weather expressions: no 'it'
grammar.body:
English says 'it is raining'; Malayalam names the actual subject:

• **മഴ പെയ്യുന്നു** 'rain falls' = it's raining
• **കാറ്റ് വീശുന്നു** 'wind blows' = it's windy
• **ഇടി വെട്ടുന്നു** 'thunder strikes' = it's thundering
• **വെയിൽ ഉണ്ട്** 'there is sunshine' = it's sunny

Temperature and conditions are nouns used with **ആണ്** or **ഉണ്ട്**, often intensified with നല്ല: നല്ല **ചൂടാണ്** 'it's hot', **തണുപ്പുണ്ട്** 'it's cold', ഈർപ്പം കൂടുതലാണ് 'it's very humid'. How a person feels uses the dative: എനിക്ക് തണുക്കുന്നു 'I feel cold', എനിക്ക് ചൂടെടുക്കുന്നു 'I feel hot'.

examples.en: It's very windy at the beach.
In April it's very hot in Kerala.
There isn't a single cloud in the sky.

grammar.title: 'Going to' and 'will probably': -ആൻ പോകുന്നു, -ും, -ുമായിരിക്കും
grammar.body:
• **-ആൻ പോകുന്നു** (-ān pōkunnu, 'is going to'): the infinitive in **-ആൻ** + പോകുന്നു. Infinitive: replace -ുക with -ആൻ: പെയ്യുക → പെയ്യാൻ, വരുക → വരാൻ, തുടങ്ങുക → തുടങ്ങാൻ. Use it for something about to happen or planned: മഴ **പെയ്യാൻ പോകുന്നു** 'it's going to rain'.
• **-ും** (-um) is the plain future: നാളെ മഴ **പെയ്യും** 'it will rain tomorrow'. With ഉണ്ട് the future is **ഉണ്ടാകും** 'there will be'.
• **-ുമായിരിക്കും** / **-ുമെന്ന് തോന്നുന്നു** 'probably will / I think it will': മഴ പെയ്യു**മായിരിക്കും** 'it'll probably rain'.

examples.en: The wind is about to pick up — close the window.
The monsoon is about to start.
There'll be thunder and lightning in the evening.
I think it's going to rain.

dialogue.title: A backwater trip?
dialogue.setting: Nisha and her visiting friend Chris plan a houseboat trip in Alappuzha.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.en: Shall we go on a boat trip on the backwaters tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: നാളെ നല്ല മഴ പെയ്യുമെന്ന് ടിവിയിൽ പറഞ്ഞു.
lines.roman: nāḷe nalla maḻa peyyumennŭ ṭiviyil paṟaññu.
lines.en: The TV said it'll rain heavily tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.en: Oh no! Has the monsoon started?

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: ജൂൺ ആയില്ലേ? ഇനി രണ്ട് മാസം മഴയാണ്.
lines.roman: jūṇ āyillē? ini raṇḍŭ māsam maḻayāṇŭ.
lines.en: It's June, isn't it? Now it's two months of rain.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.native: പക്ഷേ ഇന്ന് നല്ല വെയിലും ചൂടും ഉണ്ടല്ലോ.
lines.roman: pakṣē innŭ nalla veyilum chūṭum uṇḍallō.
lines.en: But today it's really sunny and hot.

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: നോക്ക്, ആ കാർമേഘങ്ങൾ. ഇപ്പോൾ മഴ പെയ്യാൻ പോകുന്നു.
lines.roman: nōkkŭ, ā kārmēghaṅṅaḷ. ippōḷ maḻa peyyān pōkunnu.
lines.en: Look at those dark clouds. It's about to rain now.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.en: You're right! There's thunder too. Where's the umbrella?

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: സാരമില്ല. മഴയത്ത് കായൽ കാണാൻ നല്ല ഭംഗിയാണ്. മഴ നിന്നാൽ നമുക്ക് പോകാം.
lines.roman: sāramilla. maḻayattŭ kāyal kāṇān nalla bhaṅgiyāṇŭ. maḻa ninnāl namukkŭ pōkām.
lines.en: Never mind. The backwaters look beautiful in the rain. If the rain stops, we'll go.

culture: The monsoon's arrival in Kerala around **1 June** is national news in India. Malayalis have dozens of words for rain, and many love it — sitting on the veranda with a cup of tea, watching the rain, is a classic Kerala pleasure. The month of കർക്കടകം (July–Aug) is considered the season for Ayurvedic treatment and for reading the Ramayana.

tip.title: Weather words with ആണ് / ഉണ്ട് — no 'it'
tip.body:
- There's no 'it': just the weather noun + **ആണ്** or **ഉണ്ട്**: നല്ല **ചൂടാണ്** 'it's hot', **തണുപ്പുണ്ട്** 'it's cold'.
- Negatives: **ചൂടില്ല** 'it's not hot', **തണുപ്പില്ല**.
- Before a noun 'cold' is **തണുത്ത**: തണുത്ത വെള്ളം.
- How *you* feel takes the to-form: **എനിക്ക്** തണുക്കുന്നു 'I feel cold'.

sentences.en: It's really cold today.
It's very humid in Kochi.
In summer it isn't too hot in Munnar.
Is it hot today?
No, it's not hot today.
I'm cold, turn the fan off please.
What's the weather like back home?
It's always cold in England.
Could I have some cold water? It's so hot!
The weather's nice today.

tip.title: Rain 'falls'
tip.body:
- 'It's raining' is literally 'rain falls': മഴ **പെയ്യുന്നു** (right now: **പെയ്യുന്നുണ്ട്**).
- Past **പെയ്തു** 'it rained'; future / every time **പെയ്യും**.
- Getting wet: **നനയുക** → **നനഞ്ഞു** 'got wet', **നനയും** 'will get wet'.
- 'In the rain' is **മഴയത്ത്**.

sentences.en: Is it raining now?
It rained a lot in Kochi yesterday.
In the monsoon it rains every day.
No umbrella? You'll get wet!
The kids got wet in the rain.
I didn't bring an umbrella.
Has the rain stopped? No, it's still raining.
I love the monsoon.
It's pouring — don't go out.

tip.title: 'Going to': -ആൻ പോകുന്നു
tip.body:
- About to happen: verb in **-ആൻ** + **പോകുന്നു**: പെയ്യുക → മഴ **പെയ്യാൻ പോകുന്നു** 'it's going to rain'.
- Plain future **-ഉം**: നാളെ മഴ **പെയ്യും**; 'there will be' is **ഉണ്ടാകും**.
- 'Probably' = **-ഉമായിരിക്കും**: പെയ്യുമായിരിക്കും.
- Works for people too: ഞാൻ **കുളിക്കാൻ പോകുന്നു** 'I'm going to have a bath'.

sentences.native: ഒരുപാട് മേഘങ്ങൾ ഉണ്ട്, ഇപ്പോൾ മഴ പെയ്യും.
sentences.roman: orupāṭŭ mēghaṅṅaḷ uṇḍŭ, ippōḷ maḻa peyyum.
sentences.en: There are lots of clouds, it'll rain any minute.
It'll be really sunny at midday.
There's thunder and lightning, don't go out.
I'm going to have a shower.
We're about to eat — are you coming?
There'll be wind and rain tomorrow morning.
It'll probably rain, take an umbrella.
No sun today, it's very cloudy.
It's thundering! Kids, come inside!
The bus is about to leave, hurry up!

tip.title: In the sky, in the river
tip.body:
- 'In / at' is **-ഇൽ**: കടൽ → **കടലിൽ**, പുഴ → **പുഴയിൽ**, കായൽ → **കായലിൽ**.
- Some open spaces use **-ത്ത്** instead, like പുറത്ത്: ആകാശം → **ആകാശത്ത്** 'in the sky'.
- 'To' a place is **-ഇലേക്ക്**: **മലയിലേക്ക്** 'up to the hills'.

sentences.en: There are lots of stars in the sky.
You can see the moon tonight.
The kids are bathing in the river.
Don't go into the sea, it's very windy.
There are lots of hills in Munnar.
Tomorrow let's go out on the backwaters by boat.
No sun today, it's raining.
Let's walk up to the hills.
The sky is blue, and so is the sea.

sentences.native: ആ മരത്തിന്റെ അടിയിൽ ഇരിക്കാം, വെയിൽ ഇല്ല.
sentences.roman: ā marattinde aṭiyil irikkām, veyil illa.
sentences.en: Let's sit under that tree, it's out of the sun.
What's this flower called?
Let's have our meal on a banana leaf.
There's a bird in that tree.
Which animal do you like best?
I love flowers.
Lots of birds come in the morning.
There are lots of trees in this village.
Don't feed the animals.
